title: bug: VS Code keeps a confirmed downgrade after the project re-declares verified-local in the same window session, and applies an Allow without re-reading the declaration (no task-6d5d3db2 parity)
description:
Found by architect-1dd28c7c while planning task-48bbd091 (docs) from the landed 98c81a27 code (9eca3971, at HEAD a13eb354). 98c81a27 was planned and coded before JetBrains' fix task-6d5d3db2 landed (b1e68978), so VS Code mirrors the pre-fix JetBrains behaviour. Its step-5 note does not list this edge among the accepted ones.

Evidence, moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts:
- runtimeProfile(): `if (pinnedProjects.has(key)) { return 'protected'; }` runs before declaresVerifiedLocal(...). After a human clicks Allow Downgrade (askDowngrade persists legacy), a verified-local declaration later in the same window session never re-persists protected. If the repository flips back to legacy before the restart, the next session reads legacy with no prompt.
- askDowngrade(): the `.then` callback persists legacy on exactly 'Allow Downgrade' without re-reading the declaration. The modal is not awaited, so an Allow answered after the project already re-declares verified-local, or while its project.json is unreadable, still records legacy.

JetBrains (RuntimeSelectionPolicy.profile / askDowngrade) reads the declaration before the pin and persists LEGACY only when stillWeaker(basePath) holds.

Impact is narrow, as for 6d5d3db2: a human allowed legacy once, but the later verified-local declaration is lost, so a second downgrade happens without the confirmation the epic rail requires.

Fix direction (mirror 6d5d3db2):
- On a pinned key, still read the declaration. A verified-local read persists protected when the stored record is not protected.
- In the prompt callback, persist legacy only while the declaration still reads weaker. Any read failure keeps protected.
- Keep the 98c81a27 invariants: no new top-level import (closed-require-map vm suites), storedProfile and persistProfile return before hashing when no root is set, and runtimeProfile never throws.

Files:
- moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts (runtimeProfile, askDowngrade).
- moe-vscode/tests/protected-profile-pin.test.cjs (new cases, RED first; existing cases unchanged).
- The VS Code pin sentence in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, Security Notes, **VS Code parity**. task-48bbd091 names this row there as the open difference; this row replaces that with the landed behaviour.

Serialize: dependsOn task-20a64797 (MoeDaemonClient.ts pathForms and protected-profile-pin P11), task-648a5916 (MoeDaemonClient.ts provenance) and task-48bbd091 (writes the docs sentence this row updates).

executionContract.intendedBehavior: VS Code's runtimeProfile reads .moe/project.json before its session-pin shortcut, as JetBrains has since task-6d5d3db2. So a verified-local read records the project protected even after Allow Downgrade recorded legacy earlier in the same window session, and a legacy declaration after the restart asks again. Allow re-reads the declaration and records legacy only while it still reads weaker (absent, legacy, observe or no executionProfile). An Allow answered while the project declares verified-local, or while project.json cannot be read strictly, records nothing and logs why. Unchanged: every profile runtimeProfile returns, the prompt, the store and the daemon provenance. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's VS Code Profile pin bullet states this behaviour.
acceptanceCriteria: P12, in one session. After Allow Downgrade records legacy: an unreadable declaration writes nothing; a verified-local read rewrites the record to protected; a following legacy declaration asks no second question in that session. A fresh session (a restart) with the legacy declaration answers protected and asks once.

P13 (verified-local) and P13 (an unreadable project.json): an Allow answered after the project re-declares leaves the protected record's bytes and inode unchanged. It logs 'Moe keeps the protected profile' and never 'recorded the allowed downgrade', and the next session asks again.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md is the only docs file changed, and its VS Code Profile pin bullet states the landed behaviour.
invariants: runtimeProfile never throws and returns the same profile as before for every sequence of declarations: a pinned key answers protected, a blank basePath answers legacy, and an unreadable declaration answers protected without pinning or writing.

MoeDaemonClient.ts gains no import and no top-level require (the closed-require-map vm suites). storedProfile and persistProfile stay unchanged and still return before hashing when no store root is set.

Only Allow Downgrade records legacy, and only while the declaration still reads weaker. Every other answer records nothing: a dismissal, a rejected or throwing prompt, a verified-local re-read or any read failure.
These stay byte-unchanged: the downgrade modal (message, modal flag, Keep Protected / Allow Downgrade order), ask-once-per-session, the store rules, and the spawn-provenance code.
No lock, await or timer is added: runtimeProfile and the Allow callback stay synchronous.
Pre-existing test rows, helpers and constants stay byte-unchanged.
compatibility: Profile records keep the strict {version:1, project, profile} shape, so a record written before this change reads the same.
The callers (connect, startDaemon, AgentLauncher.launch, ManagedVmTreeProvider) and their answers are unchanged. Pinned projects now re-read project.json on each call, as in JetBrains.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) A verbatim JetBrains port with recordLock: rejected. The extension host is single-threaded, and runtimeProfile and the Allow callback both run synchronously to completion, so nothing can interleave. (2) A new stillWeaker helper or closure: the architect's first two probes, both green. Replaced by the existing declaredProfile(basePath), which is the same strict read, never throws and already logs an untrusted read. That is +2 lines instead of about +10, and it keeps the edit inside askDowngrade, as the governor's placement note asks. (3) Re-reading inside the callback without a guard, so the existing .catch logs a read failure: rejected, because that line says 'the downgrade prompt failed'. (4) Clearing the session pin on a verified-local read: rejected, because the pin must hold for the whole session. (5) Mirroring JetBrains' TROUBLESHOOTING.md sentence: rejected by DoD 3 ('No other docs file changes').
